title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving WASH assistance to drought-affected rural communities in Baidoa

description.narrative: ltpgtBaidoa rural continues to bear the cumulative effects of prolonged drought, erratic rainfall, and repeated displacement. These shocks have eroded livelihoods, depleted coping mechanisms, and placed immense pressure on fragile basic services. Host communities are sharing scarce water points with newly displaced families, accelerating the collapse of already overstretched WASH infrastructure. As water sources dry up and contaminated, families are forced to rely on unprotected water sources, increasing exposure to preventable diseases and pushing vulnerable households closer to catastrophic humanitarian situation.ltbrgtWomen and girls shoulder the burden of water collection, often walking long distances to unprotected water points, exposing them to protection risks. Children under five and pregnant and lactating women face heightened health and nutrition risks as unsafe water, poor sanitation, and inadequate hygiene exacerbate diarrheal diseases. Persons with disabilities, and minority groups face persistent barriers to accessing water and sanitation due to social exclusion.ltbrgtIn response, CESDO proposes a life-saving WASH intervention with durable solutions in drought-affected host communities in 7 rural villages in Baidoa, targeting 10,482 vulnerable persons. The project will improve immediate and sustained access to safe water through rehabilitation and upgrading of boreholes, extension of water supply networks to bring water closer families and reduce travel distance, construction of water kiosks to reduce overcrowding and associated protection risks for women and girls, emergency water trucking, and operation and maintenance to support community-operated water systems.ltbrgtThe project adopts an area-based approach. Through close coordination with WASH, Health, Nutrition, and Protection actors, CESDO will ensure complementary and non-duplicative assistance, with referrals to health and nutrition services prioritized for malnourished children, pregnant and lactating women, and households affected by disease outbreaks. Centrality of Protection is mainstreamed across all activities. Community engagement will identify minority groups, persons with disabilities, and other at-risk groups, who will be actively engaged in decision-making including WASH committees and community monitoring groups.ltbrgtExclusion from assistance is proven to be a major challenge for minority and marginalized groups. CESDO will address this challenge by first conducting community mapping at the start of the project to identify clan and power dynamics in the target locations and the potential exclusion of specific groups from the assistance. Inclusive consultation sessions will be conducted with women, girls, persons with disabilities, and marginalized/minority groups. Representative and inclusive community-based committee will be established to oversee the project implementation, provide regular feedback through community meetings, and/or the toll-free hotline.ltbrgtAs an exit strategy, CESDO will train a representative and inclusive WASH committees including women, men, persons with disabilities and minority groups, with women making up at 50% of the committee members. The WASH committee will be trained on technical skills in the repair and maintenance of the WASH infrastructure, including plumbing, fixing and replacing taps. They will also play a crucial role in conflict resolution, oversee the operation of the systems and facilitate the collection of management of minimum fees for the future repair and maintenance of the established or rehabilitated WASH infrastructure. This will enhance community contribution and ownership and reduce the dependence on humanitarian assistance.ltbrgtlt/pgt
